propositions: Mutating CLI verbs (link, unlink, comment, tag, edit, set-file-impact, etc.) currently exit silently on success, making idempotent no-ops indistinguishable from writes and forcing clients to issue follow-up status queries.

Modern CLI practice and existing verb implementations (create, idea, revert, claim, session-log, transition) that print output should be normalized to a uniform one-line confirmation contract: <past-tense-verb> <args-summary> for writes and no change: <reason> for idempotent no-ops, preserving all prior data.

Global --quiet and --output flags must be extracted at the top-level router before verb dispatch to work uniformly on positional-only _REGISTRY leaves (comment, tag, untag, archive, set-verify-commands) that reject option-like tokens.
Consumed seam return values (e.g., add_dependency's dict|None REDIRECT contract) must remain type-identical and unaltered; outcome signals are added only as a parallel non-breaking channel.

link's REDIRECT record (existing machine-readable JSON output) must remain byte-identical on write and no-op, with --quiet never suppressing it, and exactly one stdout result emitted per invocation in text mode.

transition's normalized line must preserve the UNBLOCKED ids datum inside the confirmation, and all already-printing verbs (create, idea, revert, claim, session-log, transition, reopen) must retain every datum their prior output carried.
